rationale: The source contains independent obligations, each with its own trigger, evidence and reader. (1) AUTHORING: every relationship attribute on an .adoc document must name a declared doc-id. This is verified by zero unresolved-target findings. (2) RESOLVER BEHAVIOUR: build the declared-id set first, admit only declared targets, and report every other edge. Never fabricate a node and never drop an edge. This is verified by a node-count test and a reported-finding test. The resolver architecture is four separately violable obligations: (3) exactly ONE resolver; (4) it lives in this docs extension; (5) the graph is derived on demand and never persisted; (6) graph_builder.py is not reused. Round 3 changes, both from the audit: the round-2 architecture bundle is now split into parts (3) to (6), and the single-MODULE evidence is replaced by a single-IMPLEMENTATION criterion that may span several modules. Joint delivery is kept as follows. The author part requires resolve-or-report. Resolve-or-report requires each architecture part, and each architecture part requires resolve-or-report, so firing any one delivers all of them. The original remapped prerequisites are unchanged.

parts.title: Point every doc relationship at a declared doc-id

facts.note: Authored .adoc documents. The graph is derived from their attributes.
Needs a diff-level observer for :decides:/:supersedes:/:implements:/:depends-on: lines, and for corpus changes that leave existing, unchanged relationships unresolved.
Emitted by the docs_capability resolver over the whole corpus.
The task shows doc-relationship authoring or corpus restructuring.

fires: A planner adds `:implements: purpose.wortrees` (a typo), and no document declares that id.
A planner adds `:depends-on:` pointing at a document they have not written yet.
A planner deletes a document, or changes its `:doc-id:`, while other documents still name the old id.
An edit to a document that still carries an unresolved relationship attribute.
doesNotFire: A document has no relationship attributes. An absent attribute is not an unresolved edge.
Work on the resolver's own design or code. The resolver parts cover that work, and they are delivered with this part through `requires`.

parts.given: An authored .adoc corpus whose documents carry relationship attributes (`:decides:`, `:supersedes:`, `:implements:`, `:depends-on:`).
parts.when: You add or change such an attribute, edit a document that has one, or delete a document or change a `:doc-id:` that other documents may name.
parts.then: Every relationship attribute MUST name a doc-id that some document in the corpus actually declares in its `:doc-id:`.
prefer: Either declare the target, or fix the reference: `:implements: purpose.worktrees` resolves, while `purpose.wortrees` (a typo) is REPORTED.
If the target does not exist yet, the reference is premature. Author the target document first.
Use only the four shipped verbs: `decides`, `supersedes`, `implements`, `depends-on`.
avoid: Edges to a document you only intend to write. To every reader and every tool, they look the same as edges to a deleted document.
`refines`. It is deliberately not shipped (spec 2 §9 Decision 3).
unless: An absent attribute is not an unresolved edge. Only declared relationships are resolved.
parts.why: Resolve or report, never invent. A target outside the declared-id set is a REPORTED finding, never a synthesized node. This is the one hard requirement of spec 2 §5.4.
evidence: Run the docs_capability resolver over the whole corpus. Every relationship target is in the declared-id set, and there are zero unresolved-target findings.
verifier_detail: declared_id_set: the set of `:doc-id:` values read from the authored corpus, built BEFORE any edge is resolved. It is closed and enumerable, which is precisely why the documentation graph can hold a discipline the traceability graph does not.
relationship_attribute: one of the four confirmed verbs of spec 2 §5.2 (`decides`, `supersedes`, `implements`, `depends-on`). `refines` is deliberately NOT shipped (spec 2 §9 Decision 3).
Exception: an absent attribute is not an unresolved edge. Only declared relationships are resolved.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0; aliases DOCS-GRAPH-001 (via parent alias).
Source statement: the one hard requirement of spec 2 §5.4 and the flagship rule of the planner.docs extension.

parts.title: Docs-graph resolver: resolve or report, never fabricate a node

facts.note: Plans, WMBTs or acceptances that specify or change how the docs graph is built.
Needs a mapping from the docs-extension resolver code and its acceptances to these change values.

fires: A planner writes the WMBT or acceptance for the docs-graph resolver.
A change to how the resolver handles an edge whose target is not declared.
A proposal to make unresolved targets a warning, to drop them quietly, or to add a stub node for them.
doesNotFire: Pure .adoc authoring with no resolver work. .author-declared-target covers that, and it requires this part.

parts.given: The docs-graph resolver that turns .adoc relationship attributes into graph edges.
parts.when: You plan, specify or change how that resolver builds the graph.
parts.then: The resolver MUST build the declared-id set first, admit an edge only if its target is in that set, and report every other edge as a finding. It must never synthesize a node for an undeclared target and never silently drop the edge.
prefer: Write the acceptance so that it asserts the graph NODE COUNT directly, not merely the finding. An unresolved edge adds no node.
Also assert that every unresolved edge appears as a reported finding, so that none is silently dropped.
avoid: An ensure-node-on-edge pattern. In `graph_builder.py:215`, `_ensure_node` synthesizes a bare node for any unseen URN, and `add_edge` calls it on BOTH endpoints. So any edge that names a non-existent target conjures that target into being.
unless: Nothing is exempt from the no-fabrication half. There is no configuration that permits synthesis.
An absent attribute is not an unresolved edge. Only declared relationships are resolved.
parts.why: Fabrication is worse than absence. An absent parent leaves an orphan, and an orphan check catches it. A fabricated parent makes the node look CONNECTED, which defeats that check. This defect has ALREADY HAPPENED: 147 of 168 containment edges in the repository's other graph hang off invented nodes.
evidence: A resolver test asserts the graph node count directly. Adding an edge to an undeclared target leaves the node count unchanged.
The same test asserts that each unresolved edge appears as a REPORTED finding, so that none is dropped.
verifier_detail: fabrication: creating a graph node for a target no document declares, so that an edge appears to resolve. This rule exists to make that defect impossible.

declared_id_set: the set of `:doc-id:` values read from the authored corpus, built BEFORE any edge is resolved. Because the set is closed and enumerable, the documentation graph can hold this discipline when the traceability graph cannot.
Resolve or report, never invent. A target outside the set is a REPORTED finding. It is NEVER synthesized into a node, and never silently dropped.

Mechanism of the known defect, in `src/atdd/coach/utils/graph/graph_builder.py:215`: `_ensure_node` synthesizes a bare node for any URN not yet seen, and `add_edge` calls it on BOTH endpoints of every edge.

WHY FABRICATION IS WORSE THAN ABSENCE: an absent parent leaves a node orphaned, and an orphan check catches it. A fabricated parent makes the node look CONNECTED, so fabrication defeats the check more thoroughly than absence does. That is why the test asserts NODE COUNT and not merely the finding.
audit: metadata: severity 1, disposition strict (see shared:policy.strict-disposition). implementation: {type: validator, ref: docs_capability}.
This is not a stylistic preference. The defect has ALREADY HAPPENED in this repository's other graph, which is why spec 2 §5.4 states it as non-negotiable.

Reproduced live on the ATDD working tree, 2026-09-06 (#1758): total nodes 3208; fabricated nodes 44 (feature 28, wagon 6, train 6, test 4); feature -> component CONTAINS (urn-structure) 168; parent DECLARED 21 (12.5%); parent INVENTED 147 (87.5%). 147 of 168 containment edges point at features that no file declares, hanging off 28 invented nodes.

edgeRemap.reason: A target resolves only if exactly one document declares it. This matters both to the author naming a target and to the resolver admitting the edge.
The declared-id set comes from :doc-id: attributes. The author's target must be declared there, and the resolver builds the set from them before resolving any edge.
The registry is a projection of :decides: edges and is only as trustworthy as edge resolution. resolve-or-report in turn requires all four architecture parts.
